text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton called for establishing common institutions through joint efforts by local political forces in a letter to chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic.

- Head of the Croat Democratic Union's branch in Bosnia, Bozo Rajic, asks for meeting with president of the Moslem Party for Democratic Action, Alija Izetbegovic, and says current difficulties in the Moslem-Croat federation can be resolved only by a dialogue between the two leading parties.

- Bosnian ambassador to Croatia, Kasim Trnka, appeals to Bosnian refugees in the country to register for the municipal elections in September. Trnka says that there are some 100,000 Bosnian refugees who settled in Croatia and only 15,000 of them have registered so far.
- OSCE mission says if federation partners fail to form new municipalities by end of May then thousands of people will be unable to participate in the September local elections.

- Croat representatives walked out of the Moslem-Croat federation parliament session on Wednesday after their representatives accused Moslems of failing to respect an agreement worked out between the main political parties.
- Michael Steiner, deputy High Representative to Bosnia, blames the international community and local political leaders for Sarajevo's political problems.
- Moslem-Croat federation parliament failed to adopt the federation budget after opposition representatives in the parliament refused to support it.
- State-run airline Air Bosnia has become a full member of the International telecommunication system SITE, allowing communication with other airlines, officials say.
